title: Exterior sheaves commute with open restriction
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal M$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $n\geq0$, and $U\subseteq X$ an open subscheme. For the exterior sheaf defined by sheafification of sectionwise exterior powers [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power], there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules $(\bigwedge^n\mathcal M)|_U\cong\bigwedge^n(\mathcal M|_U)$. No local-freeness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For every open $V$ of $U$, restriction identifies the sections of $\mathcal M|_U$ and its scalar ring with those of $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal O_X$ on the corresponding open of $X$. Transport through the scalar-ring isomorphism and apply the universal property of exterior powers in both directions, sending every pure wedge to the same wedge of its identified factors. The composites are identities since pure wedges span. The restriction maps agree on pure wedges by [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power], hence everywhere. This gives a presheaf isomorphism between the exterior presheaf on $U$ and the restriction of the exterior presheaf on $X$.

Sheafification commutes with restriction to $U$: a section of the associated sheaf is locally represented by presheaf sections, with equal representations identified after a covering refinement; an open in $U$ has exactly the same open covers and refinements when viewed in $X$. These local representations and their equivalence relations coincide under restriction, and the scalar actions coincide as well. Consequently the associated sheaves of the two presheaves just identified are isomorphic. Composing these isomorphisms proves the assertion, including $n=0$ and $U=\varnothing$.
